title: Pigou Club
article: List of supporters of Pigouvian taxes

definition.text: The Pigou Club is economist Gregory Mankiw's name for economists and commentators who have publicly backed higher Pigouvian taxes.

facts.text: Named after Arthur Cecil Pigou, it gathers modern economists who support a carbon tax to tackle climate change.
The Economist, The Washington Post editorial board, NPR's Planet Money and The New York Times have expressed support for Pigouvian policies.

notes: Excluded: a list page of supporters, not a concept; may serve as colour under Pigouvian tax.

definition.text: A steering tax, or ecological incentive tax, is meant to change taxpayers' behaviour rather than to raise revenue.

facts.text: A Pigouvian tax is a special case of a steering tax aimed at a negative externality.
If the tax succeeds in changing behaviour, its revenue falls, so the steering aim and the revenue aim pull against each other.
Some, like the Swiss tax on volatile organic compounds, are fully paid back to the population, rewarding people who pollute less.
A Swiss study found a per-person refund is the most progressive way to return environmental tax revenue.

title: British Columbia carbon tax

definition.text: The British Columbia carbon tax, in force from 2008 until its repeal on 1 April 2025, taxed fossil fuels while cutting income and corporate taxes by about the same amount.

facts.text: It began at $10 per tonne of CO2e on 1 July 2008, the first such tax in North America, and was designed to be revenue-neutral.
It was collected at the point of retail sale, such as the gas pump, with a tax credit to protect low-income families.
The rate reached $40 per tonne in 2019 and $80 per tonne in 2024.
A 2013 review reported per-capita fossil fuel use down 17.4% while GDP growth kept pace with the rest of Canada.
A 2017 paper found a small but significant 0.74 percent annual employment increase over 2007–2013.
A 2021 counterfactual study found no significant negative impact on GDP and complete pass-through of the tax into energy prices.

contested_note: Critics argued that falling fuel use reflected cross-border shopping and a Vancouver gas levy rather than the tax.
